title: Grounding
summary: Direct skin-to-earth contact—barefoot feet or Make like the Sphinx belly contact—as the zero-hardware Magnetism habit, and how indoor mats fit beside it.

sections.heading: Why grounding is on the list
sections.body: Most of modern life is spent on insulating floors, rubber soles, and elevated buildings. Grounding here means restoring skin contact with Earth’s surface—soil, grass, sand, or stone—so charge and pressure patterns from the ground can reach the body. The practical habit is short, intentional outdoor contact in daylight when you can, not a mystical ritual. Asphalt and concrete are weaker proxies than living soil or wet sand when you have a choice.

sections.heading: Barefoot vs Make like the Sphinx
sections.body: This app logs two modes. Barefoot is standing or walking with feet on a natural surface (5 pts). Make like the Sphinx means lying prone with belly and torso on the earth for fuller contact (10 pts). Log each intentional session; duration can scale points within the cap. Both count as the same keystone—choose the mode that matches what you actually did.

sections.heading: How to practice without drama
sections.body: Pick a safe patch: yard, park, beach, or trail—not broken glass, pesticides you distrust, or traffic. Morning or midday outdoor light stacks grounding with the Light pillar. Keep sessions calm: a few minutes of real contact beats a heroic hour you never repeat. In winter or apartments, use short outdoor windows when weather allows, and treat indoor mats as a convenience layer (see the grounding-mats lesson), not a full replacement.

sections.heading: Where Dr. Jack Kruse’s teaching is specific
sections.body: Kruse’s magnetism material treats outdoor Earth contact as a non-negotiable input in the light–water–magnetism stack—often paired with sunrise light, cold, and low nnEMF at night. He frames grounding as restoring a native DC reference the built environment removed. Product mats and outlet kits appear more in community practice; his core preference is real outdoor ground. Read those prescriptions as environment design, not as a measured electron dose from this app.

sections.heading: What is solid, what is framework
sections.body: Solid ground: skin on soil is real physical contact; outdoor time also brings daylight and usually lower RF density than a dense indoor router zone; mats require electrical safety checks. Framework / teaching layer: that barefoot minutes reliably “discharge inflammation” or rewrite mitochondrial redox in a way this app can verify. Treat grounding as a daily place habit inside Magnetism—not medicine.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Log Grounding: choose Barefoot or Make like the Sphinx, then duration if prompted. Pair with Nature immersion for longer outdoor blocks and with Sleep Space / Work Space if you also use verified grounding mats indoors. Educational lifestyle tracking only—not medical advice.
